title: Grandfathered NESC Standard Versus New Development Trigger with Lapsed Budget Authority
scenario_text:
Context from SharePoint — /engineering/standards/nesc-compliance-matrix.xlsx (last modified: 2024-03-15):
Asset TL-2290-044 (Distribution pole, wood, installed 1991). Listed as 'Grandfathered — NESC 2007 edition.' Note in column K: 'Clearance to ground = 22.1 ft (meets 2007 min of 18.5 ft; does NOT meet 2023 min of 23.0 ft for new construction).'

Context from Esri ArcGIS (parcel layer + asset overlay):
Parcel 09-443-012 (adjacent to TL-2290-044) rezoned from Agricultural to Commercial on 2025-11-20. New site plan filed: 3-story mixed-use building. Structure TL-2290-044 is within 15 ft of new building envelope per site plan overlay.

Context from Outlook — email chain (Subject: 'RE: RE: 2290 pole conflict — new development on Parcel 09-443'):
From: jessica.huang@conduitenergy.com (Engineering Supervisor)
To: doug.brennan@conduitenergy.com
Date: 2026-01-08

> On Jan 5, tom.nakamura wrote:
> > Under NESC 234C2, the rezoning and proximity of new structure triggers current-edition compliance.
> > We need to relocate or raise the pole. Estimate: $185K.
>
> Doug — I confirmed with Steve Martinez (VP, Grid Ops) verbally on Thursday that this should go
> through as a capital improvement. He said 'just get it done, we'll figure out the bucket later.'

Doug — Steve approved but his delegation authority caps at $150K for unplanned capital per the 2025 delegation matrix (updated after the rate case). Anything above that needs Karen Albright (SVP, Operations) or it goes to the capital committee.

Context from SAP (Project budget system):
Blanket WO for 'Distribution Pole Replacements — 2026' | Budget: $2.4M | Spent YTD: $1.9M | Remaining: $500K | Approval authority: VP Grid Ops (Steve Martinez) for individual items up to delegation limit.

Context from Microsoft Teams — #grid-engineering (2026-01-12, 9:17 AM):
@tom.nakamura: Filed the Maximo WO for 2290-044 relocation. Tagged it to the blanket. $185K.
@jessica.huang: (checkmark emoji)
@doug.brennan: Hold on — did we get Karen's sign-off? Steve's limit changed after the rate case.
[Message edited by @doug.brennan at 9:19 AM — original text not visible]
@tom.nakamura: Steve said it's fine. He told Jessica directly.
@doug.brennan: (no reply)

Context from Custom FileMaker (Regulatory filings):
Docket CE-2025-0034: Conduit Energy 2025 rate case. Approved 2025-09-01. Exhibit 14: Updated delegation of authority matrix. Capital project approval: VP = $150K, SVP = $500K, Capital Committee = $500K+.
question: What is the correct disposition of the $185K pole relocation project given all evidence across these systems?

contributor.name: Douglas Brennan
contributor.title: Asset Integrity Manager
contributor.domain_expertise: Infrastructure inspection programs, regulatory compliance for aging assets, capital vs expense decisions

choices: The project needs capital committee approval ($500K+) because it should be combined with the existing blanket spend, making the cumulative authorization exceed SVP threshold.
The project can proceed under the grandfathered NESC 2007 standard since the pole itself is not being modified — only the adjacent parcel is changing — so no upgrade trigger exists.
The project requires SVP (Karen Albright) approval because it exceeds Steve Martinez's $150K delegation limit per the post-rate-case matrix, regardless of blanket WO availability.
The project is properly authorized — Steve Martinez has blanket WO authority over the $2.4M distribution pole replacement budget, and $185K is within the remaining $500K balance.
